faq_heading: New Westminster neighbourhoods: your questions answered

blocks.text: Draft for Jared’s approval. Figures are closed sales from Jared’s Paragon export; the neighbourhood map outlines are drawn by us and stay draft until each is confirmed.

New Westminster is split into 12 MLS® sub-areas, the neighbourhood boundaries the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® board uses for every listing and sale. From November 2025 to October 22, 2026, 797 homes sold across them: 150 houses, 568 condos and 73 townhomes and 5 duplexes. The busiest were Uptown (146), Downtown (135), Quay (128).

By median price, the houses that sold in Glenbrooke North were the most expensive of the 7 New Westminster neighbourhoods with 10 or more house sales ($1,575,000), and those in Queensborough the least ($1,264,500). For condos, the range ran from $519,900 in Downtown to $690,000 in Queensborough.

These are MLS® sub-areas, not the City of New Westminster’s planning areas, so a neighbourhood here can be larger or smaller than the name suggests. The map and tables below follow the board’s boundaries. Use them to compare areas, then ask Jared for a search set to the exact streets you care about.

blocks.source: Source: Paragon, the MLS® system used by Jared’s office, closed sales from November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026. Pending sales are not counted. Median means the middle price, so half sold for more and half for less. Sold vs list is the sale price as a percentage of the last list price. A figure is shown only where at least 5 homes sold, and a median is shown only with 5 or more sales; with fewer, one sale would be the whole figure.

items.t: New Westminster real estate market stats

faq.q: How many neighbourhoods does New Westminster have?
faq.a: The MLS® splits New Westminster into 12 sub-areas: Connaught Heights, Downtown, Fraserview, Glenbrooke North, Moody Park, Quay and 6 more. 12 have a page on this site.

faq.q: Which New Westminster neighbourhood sold the most homes?
faq.a: Uptown had the most closed sales, 146 between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, followed by Downtown (135) and Quay (128).

faq.q: Where are New Westminster houses the most and least expensive?
faq.a: Among areas with 10 or more house sales, the median was highest in Glenbrooke North at $1,575,000 and lowest in Queensborough at $1,264,500, for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.

faq.q: Which New Westminster neighbourhoods are best value for a condo?
faq.a: Median condo prices ran from $519,900 in Downtown to $690,000 in Queensborough among areas with 10 or more condo sales. Price is one measure only; compare strata fees, age and building condition too.

faq.q: Who can help me buy or sell in New Westminster?
faq.a: Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, works across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361 or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: Do I need a home inspection when buying in New Westminster?
faq.a: It is strongly recommended. Make the offer subject to an inspection so a qualified inspector can look at the roof, structure, drainage, electrical and heating before you remove conditions.

faq.q: Can I book a private showing with Jared?
faq.a: Yes. Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, books private showings across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361, or use the contact form on this site.
